Questions 24 and 25 use the following information.

Patty stacks boxes of detergent at the supermarket.
She uses a pattern like this.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 856 221" width="100%" height="auto"><image href="/selective/t2-q24-25.jpg" x="0" y="0" width="856" height="221"/></svg>

parts.stem: How many boxes does Patty need to make a stack five boxes high?

steps.work: We can try to find a mathematical pattern here. In this case, if the stack is two boxes high, we use \(2 \times 3 \div 2 + 2 = 5\). If the stack is three boxes high, we use \(3 \times 4 \div 2 + 3 = 9\), and so on. So if the stack is five boxes high, we use \(5 \times 6 \div 2 + 5 = 20\).

parts.stem: Patty has 48 boxes. Using this stacking pattern, how high is the largest stack she can make?

steps.work: If Patty has 48 boxes, we can go backwards. First, try using the answer. For example, if the stack is 8 boxes high, we must go \(48-8=40\). Now we do \(40 \times 2=80\). Testing \(8 \times 9=72\), which is quite close to 80. Now if the stack is 9 boxes high, we must do \(48-9=39\). Now we do \(39 \times 2=78\). Testing \(9 \times 10=90\), which is larger than 78. Therefore, if Patty has 48 boxes, the largest stack she can make is 8 boxes high.

steps.work: \(\$2\) worth of 20c coins is 10 coins. The diagram shows 3 coins with a total length of 31mm. Draw a diagram of 4 coins and the length of that is 39mm. A diagram of 5 coins shows the length of that as 47mm. Hence an equation can be found, as all these numbers are one less than multiples of 8. The 3 coin chain can be written as: \(8 \times 4-1\), the 4 coin chain can be written as \(8 \times 5-1\) and the 5 coin chain can be written as \(8 \times 6-1\). Therefore, a 10 coin chain can be written as \(8 \times 11-1\), which is 87mm

questions.stem: The sum of ages of 5 children born at the intervals of 3 years each is 50 years. What is the age of the youngest child?

steps.work:
Let the ages of children be \(x\), \((x + 3)\), \((x + 6)\), \((x + 9)\) and \((x + 12)\) years.

Then, \(x + (x + 3) + (x + 6) + (x + 9) + (x + 12) = 50\)

\(\Rightarrow 5x = 20\)

\(\Rightarrow x = 4\).

\(\therefore\) Age of the youngest child = \(x\) = 4 years.

questions.stem: Riya did some vocabulary tests. Excluding the mark of her last exam, her average mark was 18. In her last test, she achieved a mark of 13, which brought her average down to 17. How many tests did Riya sit altogether?

steps.work:
Let x be number of tests done.

Total after last test = \(17 \times x\)

Total before last test = \((x-1) \times 18\)

Total after last test = \((x-1) \times 18 + 13\)

\((x-1) \times 18 + 13 = 17 \times x\)

\(18x - 5 = 17x\)

\(x = 5\)

questions.stem: A reservoir is \(\frac{3}{7}\) full. If 120 litres of water is added, the reservoir is \(\frac{9}{11}\) full. What is the capacity (in litres) of the reservoir when full?

steps.work:
\(\frac{9}{11} - \frac{3}{7} = \frac{30}{77}\)

This is equal to 120 L, therefore 1/77 of the total capacity = 4 L

Total capacity = \(4 \times 77 = 308\)L
